{{ModBox}}
'''Reach''' is a [[mod]] that increases the [[range]] of a [[Melee]] weapon's attacks. [[:Category:Glaive|Glaives]] gain increased projectile size, while throw distance remains unchanged.

For the robotic companion [[Helios]], Reach increases the range at which it can attack enemies if installed on {{Weapon|Deconstructor}}.

==Stats==

==Drop Locations==
{{DropLocations}}

==Notes==
*Reach does '''not''' increase the radius of slam radial attacks.
*Reach does '''not''' increase the range limit of thrown melee weapons, but instead grants these weapons a larger hitbox.
*Reach does '''not''' increase the fall-off range for gunblade melee weapons.

==Tips==
*The effects of Reach are '''not''' seen in the energy trails that appear while swinging a weapon, but the trails themselves determine which angles would the attacks land as the new range of the equipped weapon.
*Can be installed on [[Helios]]' {{Weapon|Deconstructor}} to extend its attack range.

{{Navigation|Melee|Stance|Maneuvers|Key Bindings|Melee/Gallery}} {{Successor |precededby=Melee 1.0 |precededbysince={{ver|13}} }} {{Infobox | Box title = Melee | image = IconMelee.png }}
'''Melee''' is a combat system in [[WARFRAME]] that utilizes edged or blunt weapons and close quarter attacks. Melee weapons can be equipped in the tertiary weapon slot of the [[Arsenal]].
==Melee Classes== Current melee weapons consist of a number of classes, in which each class of weapons has a unique set of attack animations, including normal, slam, slide, [[stealth]] attacks, finishers, combos, and blocking. {{MeleeNavVisual}} {{clr}} ==Basic Maneuvers and Mechanics== Melee can be switched to at any time by pressing the melee attack key (default {{Keybind|E}}), immediately [[holster]]ing the currently equipped gun, and can instantly switch back to an equipped primary or secondary weapon with the fire button (default {{Keybind|LMB}}) or [[zoom]] (default {{Keybind|RMB}}). Going into melee mode (default holding {{Keybind|F}}) will unlock additional melee combat features such as manual [[#Blocking|Blocking]]. All melee attacks can be executed by pressing or holding the melee input button. Every attack causes the player to take a single step forward. However, if the player is crouched, non-combo melee attacks will not cause a step forward. Each melee weapon has a number of attributes, such as [[Attack Speed]] and [[Damage]]. Each attribute can be altered by a variety of [[Melee Mods]]. {{clr}} ===Normal Attack=== [[File:SwordComboNeutral.gif|thumb|Excalibur performing a basic melee combo.|right]] {{Combo|{{Keybind|E}}|ps4 = {{Keybind/PS4|circle}}}} The simplest form of melee attack. The action is achieved by simply pressing the melee attack key repeatedly, in which the animation pattern continues to loop until the player ceases the attack. Common Attributes: *[[Damage]]: Damage done by each hit. Enhanced by damage mods such as {{M|Pressure Point}}. *[[Attack Speed]]: Speed of the attack animation. Enhanced by Attack Speed mods such as {{M|Fury}}. *[[Follow Through]]: When hit multiple targets in one strike, the part of damage remaining after each target (excludes Slam Attacks and Slide Attacks). *Cleave Radius: A rough estimation of the size of the swing. May not be accurate due to individualized cleaving animations. {{clr}} ===Slide Attack=== [[File:SwordComboSlide.gif|thumb|Excalibur performing a slide attack.|right]] {{Quote|Damage inflicted on enemies when performing a Spin attack.|In-game Description}} {{Combo|While Sliding + Melee}} Air variation: {{Combo|While Air Sliding + Melee}} Also known as a Spin Attack, Slide Attacks propels a Warframe forward while performing a spinning slash around them, dealing greater damage and hitting multiple enemies. For sparring weapons like the {{Weapon|Kogake}} and {{Weapon|Obex}}, slide attacks perform a double kick that targets only a single enemy, but ragdolls them away instead of only dealing damage. Slide Attacks can be performed on the ground to hit low-lying enemies, or in the air to hit tall enemies, potentially landing headshots. Slide attack damage can be increased by the {{M|Pressure Point}} mod and all other elemental damage the player may have equipped on their weapon (e.g. {{M|Shocking Touch}}). {{clr}} ===Aerial Attack=== [[File:SwordComboAir.gif|thumb|Excalibur performing an aerial combo.|right]] {{Combo|In Air + Melee}} Press the melee attack button while in mid-air to perform an aerial attack, or rapidly press to perform an aerial attack combo, regardless if a jump has already been made or not. The Warframe will automatically maintain Aim Glide for the rest of the air combo if Aim Glide was initiated at the time of starting the combo. This is useful for fighting airborne targets such as [[Osprey]]s. {{clr}} ===Slam Attack=== [[File:SwordComboSlam.gif|thumb|Excalibur performing a slam attack.|right]] {{Quote|Damage inflicted on enemies by landing a Ground Slam attack near them.|In-game Description}} {{Quote|Ground Slam attack hits all enemies around the point of impact within (Slam Radius)m.|In-game Description}} {{Combo|In Air + Aim Downwards + Melee}} Also known as a Leap Attack, Jump Attack or Ground Slam. While in mid-air, this performs an aimable, plummeting melee strike that deals damage and usually inflicts {{D|Stagger}} to enemies in a radius that increases with the height of the drop. Melee combo is gained for each enemy struck by the slam's area of effect. A variation, the [[Heavy Slam]] attack, additionally benefits from the Heavy Attack [[combo multiplier]] and applies the {{D|Lifted}} status, but consumes [[melee combo]]. Slam attacks deal 2x weapon damage (3x for Heavy Slams), with a single element base damage composition ({{D|Impact}} typically, and {{D|Blast}} for Heavy Slams, but the element can vary depending on the weapon). Damage dealt by slam attacks is affected by [[Damage Falloff]], meaning that it diminishes linearly from 100% at the center to 50% along the outer radius (70% for Heavy Slams). Initiating a slam attack results in instantaneous velocity towards the intended point of impact. Players can utilize slam attacks to change direction or add momentum while in mid-air, effectively zip-lining themselves in the direction of the slam. Slam attacks require that the reticle be aimed downward, with a limit about 20 degrees below the horizon, or 70 degrees above nadir. If the reticle is any higher than that, an [[Melee#Aerial_Attack|Aerial Attack]] will be performed instead. ==== Slam Attack Stats By Weapon Class ==== The base size of the slam radius is determined by the class of weapon used (e.g. [[Sword]], [[Hammer]], [[Scythe]], etc.), ranging from 5 to 9 meters. The radius is increased depending on the height of the vertical drop during the slam, with the radius scaling up to a maximum '''150%''' of the base value (7.5m to 13.5m), achieved by slamming from a height of at least '''15''' meters. The minimum radius for normal slams on most weapons is 2.5 meters. The following table shows the base slam radius and height scaling of each weapon class. {| class="wikitable sortable" cellpadding="2" cellspacing="0" style="text-align:center;" |- ! scope="col" |Weapon Class ! scope="col" |Typical Normal

For example, {{Weapon|Masseter}} has a normal slam radius of '''10m''' and a heavy slam radius of '''10m''', despite Heavy Blades typically having a normal slam radius of '''8m''' and a heavy slam radius of '''9m'''. Generally speaking, minimum slam radius scaling is determined by the weapon's listed range for a normal slam, with the equation being determined by: :::{\text{Minimum Percent of Slam Radius} = \frac{2.5}{\text{Normal Slam Radius}}} So for example, {{Weapon|Tenet Exec}} scales its slams radius from :::{{Math|2.5/4|p=y|bf=y}} of its listed radius up to to '''150%''' of its listed radius. ====Slam Damage==== A unique damage multiplier called '''Slam Damage''' is applied to both normal and Heavy Slam attacks. This bonus is '''multiplicative with other modifiers to melee damage''', such as {{M|Pressure Point}}. Sources of Slam Damage include: * {{M|Seismic Wave}}: +200% Melee Slam Damage * [[Nira's Set]] bonus: +150% Slam Damage per mod equipped: {{M|Nira's Anguish}}, {{M|Nira's Hatred}}, and {{M|Nira's Contempt}}. * Melee [[Riven Mods]], when [[Riven Splicer|splicing]] the Melee Damage stat with either Attack Speed or Status Chance. ===Wall Attack=== [[File:SwordComboWall.gif|right]] {{Combo|While Wall-Latching + Melee}} While wall-latching a player may initiate a melee attack, causing the frame to drop off the wall facing the direction aimed, with a special melee attack animation. The attack will change depending on what melee weapon is used; most weapons will slash the air in front of them as they unlatch off the wall, while heavy weapons will swing the weapon beneath them, and sparring weapons will deal a forward punch. Since {{ver|26}}, Wall Attack damage stat is not shown in the Arsenal. {| class="wikitable sortable" cellpadding="2" cellspacing="0" style="text-align:center;border:1px solid black;font-size:12px;" |- ! scope="col" |Weapon Class ! scope="col" |Wall Attack Damage in Relation to Melee Damage |- |[[Blade and Whip]] | rowspan=15 | 3.0x |- |[[Dagger]] |- |[[Dual Daggers]] |- |[[Dual Nikanas]] |- |[[Dual Swords]] |- |[[Fist]] |- |[[Glaive (Weapon Type)]] |- |[[Gunblade]] |- |[[Machete (Weapon Type)]] |- |[[Rapier]] |- |[[Sparring]] |- |[[Sword and Shield]] |- |[[Nunchaku]] |- |[[Warfan]] |- |[[Whip]] |- |[[Claws (Melee)]] || ~2.98x |- |[[Nikana (Weapon Type)]] || ~2.14x |- |[[Heavy Blade]] | rowspan=5 | 2.0x |- |[[Hammer]] |- |[[Scythe]] |- |[[Sword]] |- |[[Tonfa]] |- |[[Polearm]] | rowspan=2 | ~1.666x |- |[[Staff]] |- |} {{clr}} ==Advanced Maneuvers== ===Stances=== [[File:MeleeCombos.jpg|200px|right|thumb|The Melee Combo list for the {{M|Crimson Dervish}} Stance.]] {{main|Stance}} Upon equipping a [[Stance]] Mod, up to three additional advanced '''Melee Combos''' will be unlocked, which are special chained attacks that enhance the melee abilities of the weapon. These combos can only be performed while wielding a melee weapon. The combination will vary depending on the melee weapon equipped and the Stance mod equipped. [[Maneuvers#Rolling|Dodging]] or rolling while performing melee combos will immediately end the combo, canceling the current melee animation. {{clr}} ===Blocking=== [[File:SkanaBlocking.jpg|200px|right|thumb|{{WF|Volt}} with {{Weapon|Skana}} in blocking pose.]] {{Quote|While in hand, melee weapons block incoming attacks within a [Blocking Value]° cone. Blocking is centered around the current point of aim.|In-game Description}} {{Combo|Weapon Aim {{Keybind|RMB}}|ps4={{Keybind|L2}}}} '''Blocking''' is a defensive technique that negates both incoming damage and knockbacks in an angle in front of the Warframe. Successful blocking can only be performed if enemies attack within the blocking angle cone of the player's melee weapon, which varies depending on the melee weapon type. For example, [[Dual Swords]] have a blocking angle of 60°, meaning any damage coming from 60° to the left or right of the reticle will be negated. All melee weapons block 100% of incoming damage, with the exception of certain [[boss]] attacks, as well as certain sources of area-of-effect damage such as [[Bombard]] rockets, both being cases where blocking is only partially effective. However, it does not negate [[Status Effect]]s in most instances (notable exceptions include the [[Knockdown]] and {{D|Heat}} status effects from an [[Eximus#Arson|Arson Eximus]]' ability). When a melee weapon is drawn by performing a melee attack while using a [[Weapon Comparison/Primary|primary]] or [[Weapon Comparison/Secondary|secondary]] weapon, blocking is '''automatic''' assuming enemies are attacking within the blocking angle. However, if a melee weapon is manually switched to, or only a melee weapon is equipped in the [[Arsenal]], blocking is '''manual''' and the block button must be held down to block. Any time an attack is successfully blocked, 1 point will be added to the [[#Combo|Combo Counter]]. Additionally, blocking an enemy melee attack has a chance to stagger them, briefly opening them up to [[Finisher|melee front/back finishers]]. This stagger chance can be increased through mods like {{M|Parry}}. *Blocking negates damage from [[Continuous Weapon|continuous weapons]] like {{Weapon|Flux Rifle}} lasers and [[Scorch]] flamethrowers, as well as non-continuous weapons like {{Weapon|Gorgon}} bullets and [[Butcher]] cleavers. *Blocking completely negates the knockdown effect of [[Seismic Shockwave]] from [[Grineer]] heavy units and [[Eximus]] variants. *Blocking completely negates the pull effect from [[Scorpion]] grappling hooks. *Blocking partially negates effects like [[Fire Blast (Ruk)|Fire Blast]] from [[Sargas Ruk]] and [[Rippling Shockwave]] from certain [[Corpus]] units, preventing the knockdown effect, but the player will still be pushed back. *Certain enemies such as Fusion Moa require the player to either back up slightly or aim slightly upward in order to parry their attack up close. {| class="wikitable sortable" cellpadding="2" cellspacing="0" style="text-align:center;border:1px solid black;width:40%;font-size:12px;" |- ! scope="col" |Weapon Class ! scope="col" |Typical Blocking Angle |- |[[Dagger]] | rowspan=3 | 45° |- |[[Gunblade]] |- |[[Whip]] |- |[[Dual Daggers]] | rowspan=4 | 50° |- |[[Fist]] |- |[[Hammer]] |- |[[Sparring]] |- |[[Claws (Melee)]] | rowspan=10 | 55° |- |[[Glaive (Weapon Type)]] |- |[[Heavy Blade]] |- |[[Machete (Weapon Type)]] |- |[[Nikana (Weapon Type)]] |- |[[Nunchaku]] |- |[[Polearm]] |- |[[Sword]] |- |[[Two-Handed Nikana]] |- |[[Warfan]] |- |[[Blade and Whip]] | rowspan=8 | 60° |- |[[Dual Nikanas]] |- |[[Dual Swords]] |- |[[Rapier]] |- |[[Scythe]] |- |[[Staff]] |- |[[Tonfa]] |- |Most [[Exalted Weapon|Exalted Melees]] |- |[[Heavy Scythe]] | rowspan=2 | 65° |- |{{Weapon|Iron Staff}}, {{Weapon|Iron Staff Prime}} |- |[[Sword and Shield]] || 70° |- |[[Assault Saw]] | rowspan=2 | 90° |- |{{Weapon|Diwata}}, {{Weapon|Diwata Prime}} |- |} ====Mods That Benefit From Blocking==== AmalgamJavlokMagazineWarpMod.png|link=Amalgam Javlok Magazine Warp|{{M|Amalgam Javlok Magazine Warp}}|alt=Amalgam Javlok Magazine Warp ArcanePhantasm.png|link=Arcane Phantasm|{{Arcane|Arcane Phantasm}}|alt=Arcane Phantasm FocusedDefenseMod.png|link=Focused Defense|{{M|Focused Defense}}|alt=Focused Defense GuardianDerisionMod.png|link=Guardian Derision|{{M|Guardian Derision}}|alt=Guardian Derision ParryMod.png|link=Parry|{{M|Parry}}|alt=Parry ====Tactical Dodging==== A tactical dodge or roll can be performed by [[Maneuvers#Rolling|rolling]] while blocking, allowing the player to shorten their roll distance while maintaining melee distance with enemies in combat. {{clr}} ===Combo=== {{main|Melee Combo}} {{Infobox | Box title = Melee Combo | image = ComboCounter.jpg | caption = A 50-hit Combo Counter with a 3.0x Damage Multiplier }} {{#lst:Melee Combo|intro}} ==Heavy Attack== [[File:HeavyAttack.gif|thumb|220px|An example of a Heavy Attack. Notice entire combo counter is spent.]] {{Quote|Base damage of the weapon's Heavy Attack. Damage is increased by Combo Multiplier, but consumes Combo Count.|In-game Description of Heavy Attack Damage at the Arsenal Screen}} {{Combo|Middle Mouse {{Keybind|MMB}}|ps4={{Keybind|R3}}}} Tapping {{Keybind|MMB}} with a melee weapon in hand will perform a '''Heavy Attack''', a special attack that deals significantly more damage. Heavy Attacks consume [[Melee Combo]] upon execution, in exchange for a unique damage multiplier equal to the current [[Melee_Combo#Combo_Multiplier|melee combo tier]]. This means that the '''power of a Heavy Attack directly scales''' with the '''current combo multiplier'''. For example, a Heavy Attack performed at '''4x combo multiplier''', will deal '''4x as much damage''' as the same attack performed without a combo multiplier. The trigger for activating [[Incarnon]] melee weapons is to perform a Heavy Attack while above a certain combo threshold. Weapons with unique effects, like {{Weapon|Synoid Heliocor}}, {{Weapon|Sancti Magistar}} and {{Weapon|Syam}}, often have those unique effects attached to the Heavy Attack. With the exception of {{Weapon|Diwata}}, most [[Exalted Weapons]] can perform Heavy attacks (sometimes with extra effects, like double energy waves from {{Weapon|Exalted Blade}} or an explosive projectile from {{Weapon|Ironbride}}), though [[Exalted Weapons#Pseudo-Exalted|Pseudo-Exalted]] weapons cannot. For [[Glaive_(Weapon_Type)|Glaive-type]] weapons, the Heavy attack input does not initiate an attack animation. Instead, it can be activated while the thrown weapon is in flight, resulting in an explosion that deals Heavy Attack damage and returns the weapon to the user's hand. ===Heavy Attack Damage=== The damage dealt by a Heavy Attack is calculated by multiplying the weapon's damage with a Heavy Attack Multiplier (distinct from the previously mentioned Combo Multiplier), which is given by the weapon's type, along with stats for wind-up time and any forced status effects. * For example, a {{Weapon|Fragor}} has '''200''' base damage, and is a [[Hammer]]-type weapon, meaning that its Heavy Attacks will each do '''6x''' base damage, equal to '''1,200 damage'''. * The {{Weapon|Obex}} has '''120''' base damage, and is a [[Sparring]]-type weapon with a '''12x''' multiplier on its first Heavy Attack, equal to '''1,440 damage'''. * The {{Weapon|Nikana}} has '''142''' base damage, and is [[Nikana_(Weapon_Type)|Nikana]]-type weapon with '''5x''' multiplier for '''710 damage''' on its Heavy Attack, and imparts a guaranteed {{D|Slash}} proc that will deal an additional ''1,491 {{D|Bleed}} damage over time''. Each weapon type has two Heavy Attacks: a first and second Heavy Attack, repeating in sequence. The second Heavy Attack can also be performed by tapping {{Keybind|MMB}} while sliding. The following table lists the damage values and [[status_Effect|forced procs]] for Heavy Attacks of each melee weapon type: {| class="wikitable sortable" cellpadding="2" cellspacing="0" style="text-align:center;border:1px solid black;font-size:12px;" |- ! scope="col" style="width:20%" |Weapon Class ! scope="col" style="width:25%" data-sort-type=number |Multiplier for First Heavy Attack ! scope="col" style="width:25%" data-sort-type=number |Multiplier for Second Heavy Attack (or Slide Heavy Attack) ! scope="col" style="width:10%" data-sort-type=number |Typical Wind-up Time |- |[[Assault Saw]] || 6x (3 {{mul}} 100% + 3 {{mul}} 100% {{D|Bleed}}) || 6x || 1.0s |- |[[Blade and Whip]] || 4x || 12x (3 {{mul}} 400%) || 0.4s |- |[[Claws (Melee)]] || 5x {{D|Bleed}} || 5x {{D|Bleed}} || 0.6s |- |[[Dagger]] || 5x (250% {{D|Knockback}}{{D|Bleed}} + 250%) || 5x (250% {{D|Bleed}} + 250%) || 0.4s |- |[[Dual Daggers]] || 5x (250% {{D|Bleed}} + 250% {{D|Bleed}}) || 5x (250% {{D|Bleed}} + 250% {{D|Bleed}}) || 0.5s |- |[[Dual Nikanas]] || 12x (3 {{mul}} 200% + 600%) || 6x (100% + 200% + 300%) || 1.0s |- |[[Dual Swords]] || 5x (250% + 250%) || 5x (250% + 250%) || 0.7s |- |[[Fist]] || 5x || 5x || 0.6s |- |[[Glaive (Weapon Type)]] || 2x || 3x || 0.6s |- |[[Gunblade]] || 5x || 5x || 0.4s |- |[[Hammer]] || 6x || 6x || 1.2s |- |[[Heavy Blade]] || 6x || 6x || 1.1s |- |[[Heavy Scythe]] || 6x (3 {{mul}} 200%) || 12x (2 {{mul}} 600%) || 1.0s |- |[[Machete (Weapon Type)]] || 6x (150% {{D|Bleed}} + 3 {{mul}} 150%) || 5x || 0.7s |- |[[Nikana (Weapon Type)]] || 5x {{D|Bleed}} || 5x {{D|Bleed}} || 0.5s |- |[[Nunchaku]] || 5x || 5x || 0.5s |- |[[Polearm]] || 6x || 6x || 0.9s |- |[[Rapier]] || 4.5x {{D|Bleed}} || 4.5x {{D|Bleed}} || 0.5s |- |[[Scythe]] || 6x {{D|Bleed}} || 6x {{D|Bleed}} || 1.0s |- |[[Sparring]] || 12x || 15x (3 {{mul}} 300% + 2 {{mul}} 300% {{D|Bleed}} || 0.5s |- |[[Staff]] || 5x || 5x || 0.5s |- |[[Sword]] || 5x || 5x || 0.6s |- |[[Sword and Shield]] || 5x || 5x || 0.7s |- |[[Tonfa]] || 5x (250% {{D|Bleed}} + 250% {{D|Bleed}}) || 5x (250% {{D|Bleed}} + 250% {{D|Bleed}}) || 0.7s |- |[[Two-Handed Nikana]] || 6x {{D|Bleed}} || 6x (300% {{D|Bleed}} + 300% {{D|Bleed}}) || 0.7s |- |[[Warfan]] || 5x (250% {{D|Bleed}} + 250% {{D|Bleed}}) || 5x {{D|Bleed}} || 0.5s |- |[[Whip]] || 4.5x {{D|Bleed}} || 4.5x {{D|Bleed}} || 0.4s |- |} Taken together, the damage dealt by a Heavy Attack (before factoring in [[critical hits]]) can be expressed as:

\begin{aligned} [\text{Base Damage} \times (1 + \text{Damage Mods}) \times (1 + \text{Elemental Mods})]\\ \times (\text{Heavy Attack Multiplier})\\ \times (\text{Combo Multiplier}) &= \text{Total Heavy Attack Damage} \end{aligned} Example: a Heavy Attack from {{Weapon|Paracesis}}, a [[Heavy Blade]]-type weapon, modded with {{M|Pressure Point}} and {{M|Fever Strike}} and while at 7x Combo Multiplier would deal: * \begin{aligned} [222 \times (1 + 1.2) \times (1 + 0.9)] \times 6 \times 7 &= \end{aligned} '''38,974.32 damage''' Damage from {{D|Bleed}} is dealt as 6 ticks of damage, equal to 35% of the initial blow, bypassing armor. It is increased by damage and faction mods, but not by elemental or physical damage mods. The damage from a {{D|Slash}} proc inflicted by a Heavy Attack (before crits) can be expressed as:

\begin{aligned} [\text{Base Damage} \times (1 + \text{Damage Mods}) \times (1 + \text{Faction Mods})]\\ \times (\text{Heavy Attack Multiplier})\\ \times (\text{Combo Multiplier})\\ \times (1 + \text{Faction Mods})\\ \times 0.35 \times 6 &= \text{Total Bleed Damage from a Heavy Attack} \end{aligned} Ex: the {{D|Slash}} proc from a Heavy Attack from {{Weapon|Reaper Prime}}, a [[Scythe]]-type weapon, modded with {{M|Pressure Point}} and {{M|Smite Grineer}} and while at 5x Combo Multiplier would deal a total of: * \begin{aligned} [200 \times (1 + 1.2) \times (1 + 0.3)] \times 6 \times 5 \times (1 + 0.3) \times 0.35 \times 6 &= \end{aligned} ''46,846.8 {{D|Bleed}} damage over time'', dealt in ''6 ticks of 7,807.8 damage''. In addition to forced procs, Heavy Attacks can also inflict status effects normally. Increased base damage from [[Incarnon Genesis]] is not multiplied by the Heavy Attack Multiplier, but is multiplied by the combo multiplier. ===Heavy Slams=== [[File:Furax Heavy Slam.gif|thumb|220px|A Heavy Slam {{D|Lifted|Lifts}} enemies near the point of impact for 5 seconds, using a {{Weapon|Furax Wraith}} with 4x Combo Multiplier.]] {{Quote|Heavy Slam attacks hit all enemies around the point of impact within this distance.|In-game Description of Heavy Slam radius}} While melee is equipped, tapping {{Keybind|MMB}} in mid-air will execute a '''Heavy Slam Attack''', an aimable, plummeting area strike that damages and crowd-controls enemies. Damage from Heavy Slams is calculated similarly to Heavy Attacks, except that the Heavy Attack Multiplier is always 3x weapon damage. All melee weapons use the same multiplier and animation for their Heavy Slams. Heavy Slams have a larger base radius (+1 meter) and less falloff (furthest enemies take minimum 70% damage, rather than 50%) than [[Melee#Slam_Attack|normal slam attacks]], but otherwise follow the same mechanics. The slam radius increases with vertical drop, maxing out at 150% of base radius, attainable from a 15m drop. The base radius is determined by weapon type, ranging from 6 to 10 meters, with exact details in [[Melee#Slam_Attack_Stats_By_Weapon_Class|this table]]. Enemies struck by the shockwave of a Heavy Slam attack are {{D|Lifted}}, suspending them helplessly in the air. {{D|Lifted}} has a default duration of 1 second, increased by 1 additional second for each [[Melee_Combo#Combo_Multiplier|Combo Multiplier]] on the Heavy Slam. Though normal slam attacks can be useful for level traversal when launched along a diagonal trajectory, Heavy Slam attacks may be the better option. Normal slam attacks require the reticle to be below a certain angle (approx. 20 degrees below horizon, or 70 degrees above nadir), and cannot slam if aimed above that angle (resulting in an [[Melee#Aerial_Attack|aerial]] whiff instead). When aiming a Heavy Slam above that angle, the slam is executed as if it were aimed precisely at the maximum limit, allowing for the highest possible trajectory on every slam. ===Heavy Attacks and Initial Combo=== Heavy Attack weapon builds typically include mods like {{M|Corrupt Charge}}, {{M|Galvanized Reflex}} and {{M|Ready Steel}} to increase to their [[Initial Combo]] stat. Initial Combo grants a minimum value of combo points when idle or after a combo reset. This allows builds to be geared exclusively around using Heavy Attacks, restoring spent combo multiplier with Initial Combo rather than light attacks. Heavy Attack builds with Initial Combo might also invest into Heavy Attack Efficiency to increase their rate of effective attack. ===Heavy Attack Efficiency=== {{Transclude|Melee Combo#Heavy Attack Efficiency}} ===Wind Up=== {{Quote|Time a Heavy Attack must charge up before it activates.|In-game Description}} Weapons have varying Wind-up times between activating a Heavy Attack and the actual attack being performed. For example, {{Weapon|Skana}} has a wind-up time of 0.6s, meaning the actual Heavy Attack will be performed 0.6s after tapping the {{Keybind|MMB}}. Increasing melee attack speed does '''not''' reduce the wind-up time; rather, it reduces the interval between Heavy Attacks. During this brief period, the player is free to move and maneuver with the exception of performing any other melee attack. Being knocked down will cancel the charge. While winding-up, the combo counter decay is paused. Performing a Heavy Attack is possible when the combo counter is zero, and connecting with a Heavy Attack does not add to the combo counter. There is no cap to Wind Up. Even if numbers stop changing in the arsenal after adding multiple Wind Up mods, this is due to diminishing returns and the game's number rounding system. This can be proven with an FPS animation test. Heavy Slams do not have any wind up. You occasionally have opportunities to perform faster Heavy Attacks with no cost to your Combo Counter.}} [[File:TennokaiIcon.png|right|class=light-invert]] Certain mods have the ability to invoke '''Tennokai'''. With Tennokai enabled, melee hits have a '''15%''' chance of flashing a sword icon resembling the {{Weapon|Skana Prime}} on the reticle for '''2''' seconds; performing a Heavy Attack or Heavy Slam during this flash increases its [[Wind Up]] Speed and does not consume [[Combo Counter]]. *The Wind Up Speed of Tennokai attacks is '''not''' affected by Wind Up Speed bonuses from other sources. *The Wind Up Speed applies to [[Glaive (Weapon Type)]] throws as they are Heavy Attacks, though to consume Tennokai you have to explode a glaive in flight. The first Tennokai Mod {{M|Mentor's Legacy}} is awarded from the [[Whispers in the Walls]] quest. The other Tennokai Mods are awarded from [[Rotation]] C of [[Alchemy]] missions or purchasing the [[Essential_Mod_Bundle#Essential_Tennokai_Mod_Bundle|Essential Tennokai Mod Bundle]] from the [[Market]] for {{pc|100}}; the bundle only appears after installing the [[Orbiter Segments#Melee Upgrade Segment|Melee Upgrade Segment]] obtained from the Whispers in the Walls quest. Triggering Tennokai requires directly striking an enemy, though the energy waves from {{WF|Excalibur}}'s {{A|Exalted Blade}}, and {{WF|Baruuk}}'s {{A|Serene Storm}} can also trigger Tennokai. With the exception of [[Gunblade]]s, striking multiple enemies from a single hit and multi-strike attacks do '''not''' count as hits. {{WF|Titania}}'s {{Weapon|Diwata}}, {{WF|Ash}}'s {{Weapon|Shadow Clones}}, {{WF|Atlas}}' {{Weapon|Landslide Fists}}, {{WF|Gara}}'s {{Weapon|Shattered Lash}}, and {{WF|Khora}}'s {{Weapon|Whipclaw}} cannot equip Tennokai, as they cannot use Heavy Attacks. For melee [[Incarnon]] weapons such as the {{Weapon|Praedos}}, Tennokai can be used to activate their Incarnon forms without any loss to combo counter. ===Melee Damage on Heavy Attack=== The term "Melee Damage on Heavy Attack" appears on {{M|Killing Blow}}, {{Arcane|Melee Assimilation}} and can be [[Riven Mods#Splicing|spliced]] onto [[Riven Mods]]. This bonus is additive with damage bonuses from mods like {{M|Pressure Point}}, and only applies when the attack is a Heavy Attack or Heavy Slam. {{clr}} ==Lifted Status== {{Main|Lifted}} Depending on the type of melee weapon, both light attacks and especially heavy attacks can deal different effects to enemies, such as applying {{D|Knockdown}}, {{D|Ragdoll}}, {{D|Stagger}}, or {{D|Lifted}} [[Status Effect|status]]. Surviving enemies that are struck by heavy attacks from [[Heavy Blade]]s for example, will have a guaranteed Lifted proc applied to them. However, not all melee weapons grant Lifted status on heavy attack hits. {{D|Lifted}} status suspends enemies in mid-air in a ragdolled state for a short period of time, allowing players to briefly "juggle" them in a melee combo. Besides heavy attacks, Lifted status can also be applied to enemies by performing Heavy Slam Attacks with nearly any melee weapon, lifting all enemies within that weapon's ground slam radius. The higher the combo multiplier at the time of a heavy attack or heavy slam attack, the longer enemies can stay suspended. Unlike standard status effects however, status duration bonuses do not extend the lifted duration. ==Range== {{Quote|Melee attacks hit enemies within this distance. Some Stances offer more Range using throws or lunges.|In-game Description}} Each melee weapon has a '''Range''' statistic associated with it that displays the weapon's reach in meters. The [[wikipedia:hitbox|hitbox]] of melee weapons are [[wikipedia:Stadium (geometry)|obround]] in shape, with the Range stat representing the length of the hitbox and a hidden '''Sweep Radius''' stat representing its width.{{Cite}}[https://forums.warframe.com/topic/1100191-ask-me-almost-anything-again/?do=findComment&comment=10814226 Glen's Ask Me [Almost] Anything [Again]] The Sweep Radius of most melees is 0.25 meters. Range can be increased by ({{M|Primed Reach|Primed}}) {{M|Reach}}, {{M|Spring-Loaded Blade}}, {{M|Motus Impact}}, and some [[Riven Mods]]. ParacesisUnmoddedReachHitbox.jpg|Unmodded {{Weapon|Paracesis}} ParacesisUnmoddedReachHitboxSide.jpg|Unmodded {{Weapon|Paracesis}} ParacesisModdedReachHitbox.jpg|{{Weapon|Paracesis}} with {{M|Primed Reach}}|alt=Paracesis with  Primed Reach ParacesisModdedReachHitboxSide.jpg|{{Weapon|Paracesis}} with {{M|Primed Reach}}|alt=Paracesis with  Primed Reach ==Follow Through== {{UpdateMe|Does each hand of a dual-wielded weapon (e.g. [[Fist]], [[Dual Swords]]) have their own Follow Through or is it shared?}} {{Quote|Modifies the amount of damage dealt in a single strike each time an additional enemy is hit after the first.|In-game Description}} Each melee weapon has a '''Follow Through''' statistic that tells what proportion of damage is dealt to successive targets in a single melee strike. Follow Through does not affect: *(Heavy) Slam Attacks *Any attack that shoots projectiles or deals AoE (e.g. [[Glaive (Weapon Type)]] throws and explosions) In general, if a single strike hits multiple targets, the amount of damage each target will receive will be: :{{MathText|Proportion of weapon damage {{eql}} FT(n - 1)}} Where '''n''' is the order of when an enemy is hit, and '''FT''' is the amount of Follow Through for the weapon. For example, {{Weapon|Skana}} has a Follow Through stat of 0.6 ('''FT''' = 0.6). If a single strike of Skana hits three targets, the first target to be hit ('''n''' = 1) will be dealt {{Math|0.6(1 - 1)|mt=y|p=y}} of the total damage, the second to be hit ('''n''' = 2) will be dealt {{Math|0.6(2 - 1)|mt=y|p=y}} of the total damage, and the third ('''n''' = 3) will be dealt {{Math|0.6(3 - 1)|mt=y|p=y}} of the total damage. The total damage dealt with a given Follow Through stat for a sample of enemy group sizes are as such: \text{Total Damage Multiplier Against n Number of Enemies} = \sum_{x = 1}^{n} \text{Follow Through}^{x - 1} = \frac{1 - \text{Follow Through}^n}{1 - \text{Follow Through}} For example, against a group of 3 enemies, the Skana would deal '''1 + 0.6 + 0.36 = 1.96 = 196%''' of the base damage in total, which can be calculated with the closed-form formula as \frac{1 - \text{Follow Through}^n}{1 - \text{Follow Through}} = \frac{1 - 0.6^3}{1 - 0.6} = \frac{1 - 0.216}{1 - 0.6} = \frac{0.784}{0.4} = 1.96. In general, as the number of enemies grows (i.e. '''n''' approaches \infty), the damage approaches \infty if the Follow Through is one; otherwise, the \text{Follow Through}^n term approaches zero and therefore the damage approaches \frac{1}{1 - \text{Follow Through}}. For example, against theoretically infinite enemies, the Skana's damage would approach an upper bound of \frac{1}{1 - 0.6} = 1 \div \frac{2}{5} = \frac{5}{2} = 2.5 times the base damage ('''250%'''). {| class="wikitable" |- ! rowspan="2" | Follow Through || colspan="6" | Number of Enemies Hit |- ! 1 || 2 || 3 || 5 || 10 || ∞ (infinite) |- | 0.4 || 1.00 || 1.40 || 1.56 || 1.65 || 1.66 || 1.66 |- | 0.5 || 1.00 || 1.50 || 1.75 || 1.94 || 1.99 || 2.00 |- | 0.6 || 1.00 || 1.60 || 1.96 || 2.31 || 2.48 || 2.5 |- | 0.7 || 1.00 || 1.70 || 2.19 || 2.77 || 3.24 || 3.33 |- | 0.8 || 1.00 || 1.80 || 2.44 || 3.36 || 4.46 || 5.00 |- | 0.9 || 1.00 || 1.90 || 2.71 || 4.09 || 6.51 || 10 |- | 1.0 || 1.00 || 2.00 || 3.00 || 5.00 || 10.0 || ∞ (infinite) |- |} Follow Through was added in {{ver|13}}, but was only shown in the Arsenal since {{ver|26}}.{{Cite}} {| class="wikitable sortable" cellpadding="2" cellspacing="0" style="text-align:center;border:1px solid black;width:50%;font-size:12px;" |- ! scope="col" |Weapon Class ! scope="col" |Typical Follow-through |- |[[Hammer]] | rowspan="2" |0.4 |- |[[Heavy Scythe]] |- |[[Bayonet]] | rowspan="7" |0.5 |- |[[Blade and Whip]] |- |[[Dual Swords]] |- |[[Gunblade]] |- |[[Nunchaku]] |- |[[Staff]] |- |[[Whip]] |- |[[Dual Nikanas]] | rowspan="7" |0.6 |- |[[Heavy Blade]] |- |[[Polearm]] |- |[[Scythe]] |- |[[Sword]] |- |[[Sword and Shield]] |- |[[Tonfa]] |- |[[Glaive (Weapon Type)]] | rowspan="6" |0.7 |- |[[Machete (Weapon Type)]] |- |[[Nikana (Weapon Type)]] |- |[[Rapier]] |- |[[Two-Handed Nikana]] |- |[[Warfan]] |- |[[Claws (Melee)]] | rowspan="2" |0.8 |- |[[Dual Daggers]] |- |[[Dagger]] | rowspan="3" |0.9 |- |[[Fist]] |- |[[Sparring]] |- |[[Assault Saw]] | rowspan="2" |1.0 |- |[[Exalted Weapon]] |- |} ===Exceptions=== * {{Weapon|Volnus}}/{{Weapon|Volnus Prime}} have a native value of 0.6, but this reverts to category default 0.4 when a stance mod is used. *{{Weapon|Ironbride}} has a value 0.7 instead of the category default 1.0. *{{Weapon|Magistar}}/{{Weapon|Sancti Magistar}} with [[Magistar Incarnon Genesis]] Evolution II, Perk 1 ('''Crushing Verdict''') increases their value to 0.8 with a [[Channeled Abilities|Channeled Ability]] active. *{{Weapon|Nami Solo}} with [[Nami Solo Incarnon Genesis]] Evolution III, Perk 1 ('''Lone Blade''') can increase its value to 1.0, as long as the weapon is in exclusive Melee Mode *{{Weapon|Dorrclave}} will increase its value to 1.0 for 10 attacks after 10 kills. ==Finishers== [[File:Dual_Swords_Back_Finisher.png|thumb|right|170px|Excalibur executing a Stealth Attack with Dual Swords.]] {{Main|Finisher}} Finisher attacks have custom animations and deal a very high percentage of the equipped melee weapon's total damage. Players performing finishers are immune to any kind of damage for the duration of the animation. The three types of finishers are: *Ground Finisher, on knockdowned targets * Stealth Attack, on unalerted enemies *Front- / Back-Finisher, under specific effects ==Tips== *For players wanting to specialize in melee combat, remapping the equipped melee attack key to {{Keybind|LMB}} can make performing attacks and melee combos easier and more instinctive. **There is also an option which allows the Fire button to be used when the melee is drawn using the default melee key. Players can immediately return to their other weapons by pressing the Aim/Block button, which will not block, but rather bring up the previously equipped Primary or Secondary. *While doing heavy attacks, the moment the swing does damage, immediately pressing the melee key will execute another heavy attack, this can be repeated. Connecting a second heavy attack immediately after the first will retain the current combo counter, only draining it after the second heavy strike has been swung. ==Bugs== *Successfully blocking an attack while rolling can make a player unable to attack with their melee weapon. This is usually accompanied by a slight change in camera perspective where the camera is positioned slightly down while facing upwards. This bug can be resolved by performing a roll or dodge again. *Tapping the melee key slightly before landing causes the player to slide across the ground with minimal friction for a brief period. ==History== *Some melee weapons were previously used as '''''Statsticks''''', modifying the power of a Warframe's (typically [[Pseudo exalted|pseudo-exalted]]) ability via the equipped melee mods. These melee builds often featured unconventional mods specifically for the purpose of boosting an ability, rather than for use as a traditional melee weapon. ==Media== {{VideoGallery |{{YouTube|nyE0Wbef8NQ|size=300px}} |{{YouTube|36Ejk7e04II|size=300px}} |{{YouTube|xS3Qlcmgtzo|size=300px}} }}

{{Navigation|Melee|Stance|Maneuvers|Key Bindings}} {{Infobox |Box title = Stance |image = StanceSlotU145.png |caption = Crimson Dervish in the stance slot }} '''Stance Mods''' are special [[mods]] exclusive to [[Melee 2.0|Melee]] weapons that provide bonuses and additional attack capabilities. Similar to [[Aura]] mods, Stances can be slotted into a special Stance slot on melee weapons, and they increase a weapon's mod capacity. Stance mods with a matching polarity to the stance slot will double their mod capacity bonus, while non-matching polarities will have reduced capacity bonus. Leveling up Stance mods increases the amount of additional mod capacity they provide, as well as unlocks additional '''Melee Combos''' for use. {{tocright}} ==Melee Combos== [[File:MeleeCombosU145.png|right|thumb|300px|The Melee Combo list on Crimson Dervish. Outdated as of {{ver|26}}.]] When equipped, Stances change a melee weapon's animation set and unlocks the ability to perform '''Melee Combos''' that initiate different attack patterns with the weapon. Many Melee Combos allow weapons to perform attacks they are incapable of doing without Stances, like giving single-target melee weapons like the {{Weapon|Skana}} the ability to hit multiple enemies. They may also enhance a melee weapon's attacks with special effects, from increasing the weapon's damage per hit, to forcing [[Status Effect]] procs (i.e. 100% chance for a specific proc, like {{D|Slash}}), and enhancing mobility via lunges and jumps. Melee Combos are available when a melee weapon is drawn (holding {{Keybind|F}}) and can also be performed via Quick Melee attacks when using a Primary or Secondary weapon. Melee combos are initiated by inputting different inputs of the Melee key (PC default {{Keybind|E}}, see also [[Key Bindings]]) and various other keys, for example {{Keybind|Up}} + {{Keybind|E}} {{Keybind|Up}} + {{Keybind|E}} {{Keybind|Up}} + {{Keybind|E}}, where the {{Keybind|E}} key is tapped three times in succession, whiling holding down the {{Keybind|Up}} key. As of {{ver|26}}, players can flawlessly switch between combos by changing the modifier key (i.e. forward {{Keybind|Up}} or block key {{Keybind|RMB}}) during a particular combo. An equipped Stance's Melee Combo list can be seen on the "Melee Combo" button underneath the weapon's Stance Slot in the Arsenal, or in "Melee Combos" under Options while in a mission. Many Stances have a single basic combo consisting of simply pressing the Melee Key {{Keybind|E}} in sequence, and 1-3 more advanced combos requiring multiple inputs from different keys. ===Combo Types=== {| class="wikitable" ! ! High damage multiplier. | [[File:SparringComboFinisherGround.gif|64px|Sparring Ground Finisher]] |- |} ===Notes=== *Many Melee Combos deal varying amounts of damage from a single combo, for example {{M|Crimson Dervish}}'s '''Crimson Orbit''' combo has a damage multiplier of 300% whilst some combos deal less damage in exchange for faster attacks. *Many Melee Combos perform multiple strikes from a single keypress, for example {{M|Swirling Tiger}}'s '''Winding Claws''' combo hits up to six times on the first attack. *Combos ignore crowd control effects during their animations, which helps in fighting units with powerful [[knockdown]] moves like [[Heavy Gunner]]s or [[Shockwave MOA]]s or from grapples like [[Scorpion]]s or [[Ancient Disruptor]]s. Similar to blocking, hits by knockdown/grapple attacks while facing an enemy within the block angle during a combo animation will ignore the knockdown/grapple effect. **In the event that a Warframe is knocked down in the middle of a melee combo chain, the combo can still be resumed once the Warframe initiates melee as its first move upon standing up. *Some combos feature forced [[Status Effect]] procs on certain attacks, which have a 100% chance to initiate regardless of the weapon's actual status chance or availability of damage type. Many combos, like {{M|Iron Phoenix}}'s '''Wings & Beak''' and {{M|Sundering Weave}}'s '''Rapid Current''' feature forced {{D|Impact}} proc, while others like {{M|Tranquil Cleave}}'s '''Breathless Lunge''' and {{M|Gnashing Payara}}'s '''Pincer Strike''' have forced {{D|Slash}} proc. Sometimes, an attack may force proc both {{D|Impact}} and {{D|Slash}} at the same time like in {{M|Malicious Raptor}}'s '''Jagged Gash''' combo. **Attacks may force proc {{D|Impact}}, {{D|Slash}}, and {{D|Lifted}}, or have a crowd control effect like {{D|Knockdown}} or {{D|Ragdoll}}. **Rarely, attacks may open enemies up to front/back or ground [[Finisher]]s like in the case of [[:Category:Dagger|Dagger]] heavy attacks. *Some combos provide bonus {{D|Impact}}, {{D|Puncture}}, and/or {{D|Slash}} physical damage. These bonuses multiply base physical values similar to physical mods, however they stack multiplicatively rather than additively with those mods. They often come in +10%, +25%, +50%, or +100% values. {{MathText|Physical Damage {{eql}} Base Physical {{mul}} (1 + Stance Physical Bonus) {{mul}} (1 + Modded Physical Bonus) {{mul}} Combo Damage Multiplier On Hit}} ==List of Stances== There are currently 58 available stances (+27 if stanceless combos are included), which are divided among 27 different melee weapon types. ===History=== 
*Arcane Strike was first introduced in the [[Trial]] mission [[The Law of Retribution]], which was retired in {{ver|22.14}}.
*The [[Operation: Scarlet Spear]] event sold Arcane Strike from [[Little Duck]] for 1,500 {{Resource|Scarlet Credits}}.
*The [[Operation: Orphix Venom]] event sold Arcane Strike from [[Father]] for 300 {{Resource|Phasic Cells}}.

*The [[Operation: Belly of the Beast]] event sold Arcane Strike from [[Ordis]] for 3 {{Resource|Volatile Motes}} in the first run of the event, and 4 Motes in the second, with a purchase limit of 42.
*The [[Operation: Eight Claw]] event sold Arcane Strike from [[Dominus Thrax]] in bundles of 7, costing 2 {{Resource|Dominus Aureus}}, with a purchase limit of 3 (21 Arcanes in total).

==Notes ==
*The increase in attack speed is additive to mods like {{M|Fury}}.
*Also triggers on hits by ranged weapons, Warframe powers, or sentinels.
* Arcane Strike also affects the attack speed of {{A|Exalted Blade}}, {{A|Hysteria}}, {{A|Primal Fury}}, and {{A|Blade Storm}}.
*Affects [[Archmelee]] in [[Archwing]] missions.

*Particularly effective with area effects that hit many times.
**{{WF|Vauban}}'s {{A|Bastille}}
**{{WF|Gauss}}' {{A|Thermal Sunder}}, which can be subsumed to [[Helminth]]

{{ArcaneBox}}
'''Arcane Avenger''' is an [[Arcane Enhancement]] that provides a 21% chance whenever the player receives damage to increase the '''absolute'''  [[Critical Hit|critical chance]] of all attacks by 45% for 12 seconds (additive to the final critical chance).

Can be sold for {{cc|1,000}}.

==Effect==

{{Acquisition|*Awarded for killing or capturing the [[Eidolon Hydrolyst]].
*Dropped in Rotation C of [[Orphix (Mission)|Orphix]] [[Pluto Proxima]] or [[Veil Proxima]] missions.}}

===History===
*Arcane Avenger was first introduced in the [[Trial]] mission [[The Law of Retribution]], which was retired in {{ver|22.14}}.
*The [[Operation: Scarlet Spear]] event sold Arcane Avenger from [[Little Duck]] for 2,000 {{Resource|Scarlet Credits}}.
*The [[Operation: Orphix Venom]] event sold Arcane Avenger from [[Father]] for 400 {{Resource|Phasic Cells}}.
*The [[Operation: Gargoyle's Cry]] event sold Arcane Avenger from the [[Jahu Gargoyle|Vigile Jahu Gargoyle]] for 6 {{Resource|Grotesque Splinter}}.
*The [[Operation: Belly of the Beast]] event sold Arcane Avenger from [[Ordis]] for 5 {{Resource|Volatile Motes}} in the first run of the event, and 6 Motes in the second, with a purchase limit of 42.
*The [[Operation: Eight Claw]] event sold Arcane Avenger from [[Dominus Thrax]] in bundles of 7, costing 4 {{Resource|Dominus Aureus}}, with a purchase limit of 3 (21 Arcanes in total).

==Notes==
*Capable of making some abilities crit. {{main|Universal Weapon Bonuses}}
*A Rank 5 '''Arcane Avenger''' adds 45 ''percentage points'' to a weapon's critical chance after other bonuses.
*'''Arcane Avenger''' stacks additively with other percentage point bonuses, such as {{A|Covenant}} and {{M|Cat's Eye}}. For example, an {{Weapon|Atterax}} with a max rank {{M|True Steel}}, {{M|Cat's Eye}}, and '''Arcane Avenger''', will have a {{Math|[25% {{mul}} (1 + 120%) + 60% + 45%]|mt = y|p = y}} critical chance on attacks.
**Highly effective with weapons with high critical damage multipliers.
**Weapons that have 0% [[critical chance]] can crit with this enhancement, although due to their lack of a [[critical multiplier]], their damage will not be altered unless the shot lands on the head, which yields 2x [[critical multiplier]].
*Aside from damage to shields and health, this Arcane can be triggered by the following instances of damage:
**Damage to player [[Overguard]].
**Self-damage from {{M|Combat Discipline}}.
**Damage while the player is invulnerable, such as {{A|Absorb}}.
*Damage that is rounded down to 0 due to damage reduction or redirection ''can'' trigger this Arcane.
**For example, with a Rank 0 {{M|Combat Discipline}} equipped and {{A|Eclipse}} active for 75% damage '''reduction''', kills will deal {{Math|[1 {{mul}} (1 - 75%)]|mt = y}} self-damage, which is rounded down to 0, but this Arcane can still trigger.
**For example, with a Rank 2 {{M|Combat Discipline}} equipped while on {{A|Merulina}} providing 90% damage '''redirection''', kills will deal {{Math|[4 {{mul}} (1 - 90%)]|mt = y}} self-damage, which is rounded down to 0, but this Arcane can still trigger.
*Damage while {{A|Mesmer Skin}} or {{M|Mesmer Shield}} is active will ''not'' trigger this Arcane, unless {{M|Combat Discipline}} is equipped.
*Damage from {{M|Despoil}} does not trigger this Arcane.
*Damage from the {{Weapon|Hema}} or {{Weapon|Coda Hema}}'s reload does not trigger this Arcane.

{{ModBox}}
{{For|a detailed overview of CO mechanics|Condition Overload (Mechanic)}}

'''Condition Overload''' is a melee mod that grants extra damage based on the number of unique [[Status Effect|status effects]] currently affecting the target.

==Stats==

==Drop Locations==

==Notes==
*This damage does not apply to '''Slams''', '''Heavy Slams''', or Radial Attack explosions (eg. **Glaive Heavy Attacks**).
*There is no limit to the number of status effects the mod is affected by.
*The bonus damage gained by this mod stacks additively with other damage mods like {{M|Pressure Point}} and {{M|Spoiled Strike}} to increase your melee damage (including proc damage like {{D|Slash}}). Total damage is calculated as such:
:{{MathText| Total Damage {{eql}} Base Damage {{mul}} [1 + Damage Mods + (Condition Overload Multiplier {{mul}} n)] {{mul}} (1 + Elemental Mods)}} (with n being the number of unique status effects currently affecting the enemy)
*The bonus damage of a new status effect is '''not''' applied to the hit which inflicted it (or its proc damage) – only subsequent strikes are amplified.
**[[:Category:Gunblade|Gunblades']] pellets hit consecutively and therefore '''can''' be amplified by other pellets of the same shot.
*Status procs may originate from any source, including primary and secondary weapons, [[Warframe]] abilities, companions, other players, or the environment.
*{{D|Impact}}, {{D|Puncture}}, {{D|Slash}}, {{D|Cold}}, {{D|Electricity}}, {{D|Heat}}, {{D|Toxin}}, {{D|Blast}}, {{D|Corrosive}}, {{D|Gas}}, {{D|Magnetic}}, {{D|Radiation}}, {{D|Viral}}, {{D|Void}} and {{D|Tau}} procs all count for the damage bonus. Additionally:
**{{D|Lifted}} from [[Melee#Heavy Attack|Melee Heavy Attacks]] also counts.
**{{D|Microwave}} from {{Weapon|Nukor}} and {{Weapon|Kuva Nukor}} is a unique invisible status. Microwave procs have infinite duration.
**{{D|Knockdown}} while does not incur a visible status, still counts towards the damage bonus.
***Note that conditions or abilities that prevent knockdowns (e.g. {{A|Bastille}}) will prevent it from increasing damage.
**Since {{D|Lifted}} and [[knockdown]] will cancel out each other, the maximum number of status effects that can be applied to an enemy is 16.
*Radial status effects ({{D|Blast}}, {{D|Electricity}} and {{D|Gas}}) still get the bonus damage from this mod as it is part of [[Status_Effect#DoT_Damage_Scaling|Modded Base Damage]], and it is calculated based on the initial target, not individually per enemy hit.

==Tips==
*Some Melee Weapons special attacks have a multiplicative scaling with other additive bonuses such as {{M|Pressure Point}}. See [[Condition Overload (Mechanic)]] for further details.
*To achieve a high amount of distinct status procs, it is advised to use melee weapons that feature high attack speed with high base [[status chance]] and all physical damage types like the {{Weapon|Lesion}} or {{Weapon|Ceti Lacera}}.
*For complementary ranged weapons, it is advised to use weapons that feature high fire rate or area of effect with innate elemental status, such as {{Weapon|Staticor}} or {{Weapon|Pox}}.
*{{Weapon|Cedo}}'s [[Alternate Fire]] can innately proc {{D|Toxin}}, {{D|Cold}}, {{D|Electricity}}, {{D|Heat}}, and {{D|Blast}} in an area of effect along with {{D|Slash}} from direct contact with its projectile, in addition to other modded elements.
*Certain Warframes can also inflict status and/or add damage type (plus status) to weapon's attacks, such as {{WF|Saryn}}, {{WF|Ember}}, {{WF|Volt}}, {{WF|Equinox}} or {{WF|Oberon}}.
**Saryn's passive, in particular, extends the duration of any status effect she inflicts, giving her a larger time window to exploit Condition Overload's added damage.
*{{WF|Lavos}}' [[Lavos/Abilities|passive]] allows him to spread multiple status types through his abilities.
*{{WF|Voruna}}'s {{A|Fangs of Raksh}} applies 5 randomly selected status effects.
*{{WF|Citrine}}'s {{A|Fractured Blast}} applies {{D|Impact}} and {{D|Slash}} and her {{A|Prismatic Gem}} procs {{D|Heat}}, {{D|Electricity}}, {{D|Cold}}, and {{D|Toxin}} while also increasing her and her ally's [[Status Chance]] and [[Status Duration]].
*[[Sentinel]]s and their weapons are additional, viable sources for status effects:
**[[Diriga]]'s {{M|Arc Coil}} and {{M|Electro Pulse}} can cause {{D|Electricity}} procs.
**{{Weapon|Sweeper}} ({{Weapon|Sweeper Prime|Prime}}) can reliably proc statuses, even on multiple enemies with increased spread and multishot.
**{{Weapon|Artax}}'s attacks are guaranteed to proc {{D|Cold}} which also adds the advantage of slowing enemies down.
**{{Weapon|Cryotra}}'s beam can reliably apply two status effects.
**{{Weapon|Helstrum}}'s attacks in a proc setup can quite reliably apply {{D|Impact}}, {{D|Heat}} and a combo element within its AoE radius, and {{D|Puncture}} to anything directly struck by the missiles.
**{{Weapon|Prisma Burst Laser}}, obtained by purchasing [[Prisma Shade]] from [[Baro Ki'Teer]], has a reload speed of 0.01 seconds, meaning it will effectively fire without stopping, making it useful for applying status effects.
*Several weapons can wield up to 6 effects simultaneously. {{Weapon|Pathocyst}}, {{Weapon|Keratinos}}, {{Weapon|Caustacyst}}, {{Weapon|Tatsu}}, [[Plague Kripath]] and [[Plague Keewar]] [[Zaw|Zaws]], and {{Weapon|Kuva Shildeg}} with {{D|Radiation}} or {{D|Magnetic}}​​​​​ all tie for the highest number of damage types on a single melee weapon, thanks to innate secondary elements {{D|Viral}}, {{D|Radiation}}, and {{D|Corrosive}} alongside all 3 physical damage types. After modding these weapons can have up to 6 damage types, which can rise further with stance effects.
*As this is a rare mod to farm, the easiest way to farm this mod is to just keep doing Deimos Bounties and killing Thrashers and such other creatures that drop this mod.

sources.title: Damage
sources.text:
{{Navigation|Damage|Damage/Calculation|Damage/Overview Table}} {{Successor |precededby=Damage 2.0 |precededbysince={{ver|36}} }} {{Infobox | Box title = Damage | image = DamageModBundleIcon.png }} '''Damage''' (version 3.0) is a system that determines the damage done to a certain target by a given attacker. Damage results are modified by several mechanics – [[Damage Type Modifier|damage type modifiers]] (main content of this article), [[armor]], [[Critical Hit|critical hit bonuses]], [[stealth|stealth bonuses]], [[Warframes|Warframe ability debuffs]], [[Enemy Body Parts|body part modifiers]], [[Faction Damage Mods|faction modifiers]], and other sources of [[Damage Reduction|damage reduction]] – which are discussed below and on their respective pages. All damage dealt by any weapon or ability belongs to a certain damage type, and every target has specific resistances and vulnerabilities to different damage types. In-game, enemy resistances and vulnerabilities can be seen in the player's [[Codex]] after scanning at least one enemy of a particular type or by aiming at an enemy using the [[Synthesis Scanner]] with the ''Data-Parse Widget''. Exploiting enemy vulnerabilities and avoiding resistances by means of weapon selection and mod installation may significantly improve players' damage output. Since its predecessor [[Damage 2.0]], all different Health, Armor, and Shield types have been simplified into one type for each (e.g. Grineer's {{D|Cloned Flesh}} and {{D|Machinery}} is now just "Health", {{D|Ferrite Armor}} and {{D|Alloy Armor}} is now just "Armor", and {{D|Shield}} and {{D|Proto Shield}} is now just "Shield"). Vulnerabilities and resistances have also been decoupled from health types and are now solely based on the enemy [[Faction]] (e.g. all {{D|Grineer}} are now exclusively vulnerable to {{D|Impact}} and {{D|Corrosive}} at all times, regardless of the presence of armor or shields, and no longer have any resistances). ==Damage Display== {{Main|Damage Numbers}} [[File:Crit_numbers.png|thumb|Three different color tiers of critical hits along with normal damage color]] Damage dealt from players to enemies is displayed on the [[HUD]] as numbers near the point of impact on an enemy. Damage dealt from enemies to players is displayed on the HUD both as a bent strip to indicate its direction of origin and as a reduction in shield or health [[Hit Points]] to indicate its quantity. Each individual projectile or melee attack will display a single damage instance whose value is rounded to the nearest integer. Weapons with multiple projectiles like shotguns or rifles with [[Multishot]] will display a damage instance for each individual projectile. Weapons that fire continuously will display a damage instance at a constant rate depending on the fire rate of the weapon. Damage indicators are color-coded using the following system (default UI colors): * Damage appears by default in white (◼). * [[Ability]] damage appears by default in purple (◼). * [[Critical Hit|Critical hits]], also called 'Base Critical Hits', and [[stealth|stealth attacks]] are in yellow (◼). * [[Critical Hit#Critical Levels|Orange crits]], also called 'Big Critical Hits', appear in orange (◼). These are stronger than yellow crits. * [[Critical Hit#Critical Levels|Red crits]], also called 'Super Critical Hits', as their name suggests, appear in red (◼). These are stronger than orange crits. * Damage against [[shields]] and [[overshields]] appears in blue (◼), regardless of other factors such as critical hits. * Attempts to damage an invulnerable enemy appear in grey (◼). ==Overview Table== {{Transclude|Damage/Overview Table}} ==Damage Types== Every weapon, ability or method of dealing damage is classified as one or more types of damage. Through mods or abilities, further types of damage can be added to attacks. When multiple damage types are present on an attack, all of them will deal their respective amounts independent of each other, but only one damage number calculated from the combined value of the damage types will show. With each shown damage value, there is also a chance of a [[Status Effect]] occurring; the likelihood of which type of damage this Status Effect is based on depends on the percent distribution of the damage types on the weapon. ===Physical Damage=== Most weapons' base damage is made up of a combination of three physical damage types: {{D|Impact}}, {{D|Puncture}}, and {{D|Slash}}. The overall physical damage of any given weapon is the sum of Impact, Puncture, and Slash damage. This is sometimes referred to as '''IPS'''. {| class="wikitable" ! Damage Type ! Damage Type Internal Name ! Status Effect Internal Name ! [[Status Chance|Status Effects]] |- | {{D|Impact}} | DT_IMPACT | PT_KNOCKBACK | {{D|Knockback}}
Universal: Causes target to flinch and staggers movement for '''1''' second with higher stacks causing longer stagger duration. For '''6''' seconds, increases the health threshold for a [[Parazon]] finisher by '''8%''' per stack, up to 5 stacks for '''80%''' ('''100%''' on Corpus with all their shields removed) of their total health. Each stack has its own duration. |- | {{D|Puncture}} | DT_PUNCTURE | PT_FRAILTY | {{D|Weakened}}
Universal: Reduces damage dealt by the target by '''40%''' and increases received [[Critical Chance]] by '''5%''' for '''6''' seconds. Subsequent Puncture Status effects add '''+10%''' weakening, leading to up to '''80%''' reduced damage and '''25%''' critical chance at 5 stacks. Each stack has its own duration. |- | {{D|Slash}} | DT_SLASH | PT_BLEEDING | {{D|Bleed}}
Universal: Deals '''35%''' of the base damage as [[Damage/Cinematic Damage|Cinematic]] damage per second for '''6''' seconds after a '''1''' second delay. Stacks are not limited. Each stack has its own duration. |- |} Although most weapons have varying proportions of {{D|Impact}}, {{D|Puncture}}, and {{D|Slash}}, some weapons (such as the {{Weapon|Glaxion}} or {{Weapon|Phage}}) can have no physical damage at all. Other weapons (like the {{Weapon|Plinx}} or {{Weapon|Tysis}}) can deal a combination of physical and elemental, or combo elemental damage. Unlike elemental, or combo elemental damage types which can be added via mods, physical damage '''cannot''' be added to weapons already lacking them. Adding a physical damage mod to a weapon (such as {{M|Razor Shot}} or {{M|Heavy Trauma}}) specifies a physical damage type, and '''only''' increases damage matching that type. The effect of a mod can be calculated by taking the weapon's base damage, multiplying the percent distribution of the matching damage type, and multiplying again with the mod's value. The more a weapon's damage distribution is concentrated around one physical damage type, the more effective physical mods of that type become. Take for example, {{M|Piercing Hit}}, which adds 90% {{D|Puncture}} damage: * Applied to the {{Weapon|Reconifex}}, which deals 40 base damage (60% {{D|Puncture}}), it adds 21.6 {{D|Puncture}} damage. * Applied to the {{Weapon|Supra Vandal}}, which deals 40 base damage (75% {{D|Puncture}}), it adds 27 {{D|Puncture}} damage. * Applied to the {{Weapon|AX-52}}, which deals 40 base damage (100% {{D|Puncture}}), it adds 36 {{D|Puncture}} damage, and is at maximum effectiveness. This is in contrast with elemental mods, which are always applied at 100% value, even if the element is completely new to the weapon. This makes elemental mods the more flexible option for increasing weapon damage. If a weapon has >75% damage from one physical type, like {{Weapon|Desert Wind}}, then rare mods like {{M|Collision Force}} with 120% physical damage offer greater damage than typical 90% elemental damage mods. However, this edge is lost once [[Primed Mods|Primed]] versions are factored in, both because Primed elemental and physical mods have the same numerical values, and because more elemental mods have been Primed. General damage increasing mods such as {{M|Serration}} affect '''all''' the damage types of a weapon. Additionally, [[Faction Damage Mods]] such as {{M|Expel Grineer}} also affect damage as a total damage multiplier against the faction in question. ===Elemental Damage=== Elemental Damage can be applied on top of a weapon's base damage depending on what Elemental Mods are applied. Elemental Damage is applied in addition to a weapon's physical damage types. '''Weapon Damage = ({{D|Impact}} + {{D|Puncture}} + {{D|Slash}}) + (Elemental Damage Types)''' Note that a primary elemental damage type that has been combined into a secondary type will no longer be dealt to the weapon's targets, nor its status effect will be applied to the targets either. For example, a weapon dealing {{D|Blast}} damage that is created by combining {{D|Cold}} + {{D|Heat}} will no longer deal {{D|Cold}} damage or cause its '''Freeze''' effect, nor {{D|Heat}} damage or its '''Ignite''' effect to this weapon's targets. ====Primary Elemental Damage==== There are four primary Elemental Damage types: {{D|Heat}}, {{D|Cold}}, {{D|Electricity}}, and {{D|Toxin}}. A single primary Elemental Damage type can be applied alone, but if a second primary Elemental Damage type is introduced they will combine into a secondary Elemental Damage type. {| class="wikitable" ! Damage Type ! Damage Type Internal Name ! Status Effect Internal Name ! [[Status Chance|Status Effects]] |- | {{D|Heat}} | DT_FIRE | PT_IMMOLATION | {{D|Ignite}}
On Enemy: Deals '''50%''' of the base damage as {{D|Heat}} damage per second over '''6''' seconds after a '''1''' second delay (can be refreshed) while causing the target to panic for '''4''' seconds and stripping up to '''50% '''[[Armor]] over '''2''' seconds. Stacks are not limited.
On Player: Deals '''50%''' base {{D|Heat}} damage over '''6''' seconds and strips up to '''50%''' Armor over '''2''' seconds. |- | {{D|Cold}} | DT_FREEZE | PT_CHILLED | {{D|Freeze}}
On Enemy: Reduces Movement Speed, [[Fire Rate]], and [[Attack Speed]] by '''50%''', and increases [[Critical Multiplier]] received by '''+0.1''', for '''6''' seconds. Stacks up to '''10''' times, with subsequent procs increasing slow by '''5%''' to a total of '''90%''', and critical multiplier by '''+0.05''' to a total of '''+0.5'''. Each stack has its own duration. On the 10th stack, the enemy becomes Frozen for '''3''' seconds, completely freezing them in place, negating [[Shield]] recharge, and increases critical multiplier by '''+1.0'''; upon thawing, 3 {{D|Cold}} stacks will remain.
On Player: Reduces Movement Speed, Fire Rate, and Attack Speed by '''25%''' for '''6''' seconds. |- | {{D|Electricity}} | DT_ELECTRICITY | PT_ELECTROCUTION | {{D|Tesla Chain}}

On Player: Reduces armor by '''26%''' for '''8''' seconds. |- |} ====Modding==== '''Elemental Damage Combinations''' are made by following a mod placement hierarchy. This hierarchy is from closest to top left (first to be considered) to the bottom right (last to be considered) on the mod layout. Innate weapon elemental damages are considered the very last in any hierarchy, with one exception: some Kuva and Tenet weapons from [[Kuva Lich]]es or [[Sisters of Parvos]] are capable of having two base elemental damages (one from the weapon, one from the Valence damage of the Progenitor Warframe that made the Lich/Sister). In these cases, whichever of the two primary elements comes first in this element order - {{D|Heat}} > {{D|Cold}} > {{D|Electricity}} > {{D|Toxin}}, or '''"HCET"''' for short - will be placed second to last in the element combine order, while the other primary element will be placed last in the combine order. However, a weapon's innate elemental damage can be forced into a different position in the hierarchy (and thus be combined into a secondary element earlier) if the player has equipped a mod of the same element as the innate element. As well, when using multiple mods with the same element, the first position that element is placed in establishes its hierarchy and where it's combined. For example, putting {{M|Stormbringer}} on the top left slot of an {{Weapon|Amprex}} will change the position of its innate {{D|Electricity}} damage from last in hierarchy to first in hierarchy. Similarly, placing {{M|Thermite Rounds}} earlier in the hierarchy before placing {{M|Hellfire}} will still count the {{D|Heat}} damage where it was first placed. A weapon's innate elemental damage will contribute to elemental combinations, as long as the combination has been established earlier in the hierarchy. It can also combine with the last uncombined elemental mod in the hierarchy to form a secondary element. [[File:LoadOrder.png|thumb|left|Load Order]] For example: when modding a weapon with {{D|Electricity}} such as the {{Weapon|Prova}} or the {{Weapon|Lecta}}, then adding {{D|Cold}}, {{D|Toxin}}, and {{D|Heat}} in 1, 2 and 3 respectively get: {{D|Viral}} ({{D|Cold}} + {{D|Toxin}}) and {{D|Radiation}} ({{D|Heat}} + {{D|Electricity}}). In the case of [[Riven Mods]] where there is more than one elemental stat present, the hierarchy priority will be given to the '''last''' elemental stat listed on the Riven mod. For example, a Riven mod with a bonus of +100% {{D|Electricity}} damage first and +90% {{D|Toxin}} damage last, will enable the {{D|Toxin}} damage to combine with an elemental mod higher up in the hierarchy, and the {{D|Electricity}} damage will combine with an elemental damage type lower in the hierarchy. If no other elemental damage mods are present, the elements on the Riven mod will combine with itself. Weapons with innate secondary elements such as {{Weapon|Ogris}} ({{D|Blast}}), {{Weapon|Penta}} ({{D|Blast}}), {{Weapon|Stug}} ({{D|Corrosive}}), {{Weapon|Nukor}} ({{D|Radiation}}) and {{Weapon|Detron}} ({{D|Radiation}}) will '''always''' have that damage type, regardless of mods used. On weapons like these, basic elemental damage mods will combine and function ''independently'' of the innate secondary elements, as basic elements '''cannot''' combine with a weapon's already combined innate damage type. [[Kuva Weapons]] and [[Tenet Weapons]] will follow this behavior too. For example, a {{Weapon|Tenet Detron}} ({{D|Radiation}}) can come with an additional {{D|Electricity}} Progenitor damage bonus that will '''not''' add onto the innate {{D|Radiation}} damage. {{ArcaneBox}}'''Melee Doughty''' is an [[Arcane Enhancement]] for Melee weapons that increases [[Critical Multiplier]] dependent on {{D|Puncture}} status chance. ==Effect== {| class="emodtable" |- !Rank ![[Critical Multiplier#Critical Damage (Critical Multiplier)|Critical Multiplier]] !Per {{D|Puncture}} Status Chance |- | 0 || 0.5x || 10% |- | 1 || 0.6x || 10% |- | 2 || 0.7x || 10% |- | 3 || 0.8x || 10% |- | 4 || 0.9x || 10% |- | 5 || 1.0x || 10% |- |} {{Acquisition|*Can be bought from [[Eleanor]] of {{Faction|The Hex}} for {{sc|7,500}} at '''Rank 2 - Fresh Slice'''. *Rewarded from the [[1999 Calendar]]. *Rewarded from Techrot Safes in [[Höllvania]] missions. *Rewarded from Scaldra Caches in Höllvania [[Exterminate]] missions. *Dropped by the {{E|H-09 Efervon Tank}} in Höllvania [[Assassination]] missions. *Rewarded from Höllvania [[Faceoff]] missions. *Dropped by the {{E|Scaldra Screamer}} in Höllvania [[Stage Defense]] missions.}} ==Notes== *Bonus Critical Multiplier is determined by the following:
